title: Measuring Context-Dependent Cost-Benefit Decision-Making in Humans
author: Rakocevic, Alcalá, et al.

steps.title: Prepare experimental setup
steps.instruction: Install the decision‑making application on the computer or phone, configure the PostgreSQL database connection, decide how many stories each participant will answer, select which story categories will be available, and set up any optional physiological devices (e.g., heart‑rate monitor, eye‑tracker).

steps.title: Collect demographic and state data
steps.instruction: At the start of the session, have the moderator input a randomized participant ID, record demographic information, and ask the participant to rate their current hunger, tiredness, pain, and stress levels, each on a 0–100 scale.

steps.title: Select relevant story topics
steps.instruction: Present the participant with a list of story topics and let them select the topics that are relevant to them; the application will later present only stories from these selected topics.

steps.title: Set number of stories
steps.instruction: Enter the number of stories the participant will complete in the current session.

steps.title: Present story and rate rewards
steps.instruction: Show the participant the chosen story context, then display six potential reward options related to that context; have the participant assign each a unique rating from 0 to 100 reflecting how pleasant the reward would be (no two options may share the same value).

steps.title: Rate cost options
steps.instruction: Display six potential cost options related to the story context; have the participant assign each a unique rating from 0 to 100 reflecting how unpleasant the cost would be (no two options may share the same value).

steps.title: Select four equidistant rewards and costs
steps.instruction: Algorithmically choose four of the six rewards and four of the six costs such that their ratings are as equidistant as possible and span the full 0–100 range; assign each selected reward and cost a level from 1 to 4.

steps.title: Present 16 offer trials
steps.instruction: Pair each of the four selected rewards with each of the four selected costs to create 16 unique reward‑cost offers, randomize the order, and present each offer to the participant; for each offer, have the participant indicate likelihood of acceptance on a sliding scale from 0 (never accept) to 100 (always accept).

steps.title: Re‑evaluate preferences if needed
steps.instruction: After the 16 trials, ask the participant whether they wish to adjust their original reward or cost ratings; if they choose to do so, return them to the original rating screens, record the new ratings alongside the original ones, and upload both to the database.

steps.title: Rate story relevance
steps.instruction: Ask the participant to rate how relevant the story was to them on a 0–100 scale.

steps.title: Add moderator notes and close session
steps.instruction: Allow the moderator to enter any notes about the experiment; ensure that all trial data, preference ratings, relevance rating, and moderator notes are automatically written to the PostgreSQL database, then close the session.
